facts.claim: Elounda SA Hotels & Resorts (Elounda, Crete) publishes a wedding packages PDF covering civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies. The civil and Orthodox package is called the Lavish Wedding Package; the symbolic option is the Symbolic Ceremony / Renewal of Vows Wedding Package.

Elounda SA Lavish Wedding Package (civil and Orthodox) includes reservation of the wedding date and time, choice of ceremony venue, documentation assistance and settlement of the wedding licence in coordination with the couple and the local Municipality Office, a complimentary room upgrade and early check-in on arrival (subject to availability), complimentary use of the Six Senses Spa thalassotherapy pool and thermal suite for the couple, and a tasting of the chosen wedding menu for up to two people (beverages excluded).

Elounda SA Lavish Wedding Package, on the day: two witnesses if needed, ceremony set-up with a table and seasonal flower display, bride's bouquet and groom's boutonniere, rose petals, a separate room for the groom to change, a pre-recorded ceremony playlist, champagne in the bride's room and a bottle in the groom's room while getting ready, transfer of the couple to the ceremony spot within the hotel grounds, a short fireworks display and room decoration with flowers and petals after the ceremony.

Elounda SA Lavish Wedding Package, after the day: champagne breakfast in bed, a round-trip transfer to the Registry Office for the registration and certificate with the help of a hotel executive, and late check-out on departure subject to availability.

Elounda SA states the package rate does not include the Municipal fee (civil) or the Metropolis fee (Orthodox); these are charged on top and are subject to change. Package prices are published in the PDF.
Elounda SA requirement: every package is valid only if the couple stays a minimum of three nights in one of the group's hotels.

Elounda SA Symbolic Ceremony / Renewal of Vows package includes reservation of the date and time, bridal bouquet and boutonniere, two witnesses if needed and the hotel's official representative at the ceremony, a bottle of sparkling wine and a single-tier wedding cake for the couple, room decoration with flowers and petals, spa thermal suite use for the couple and breakfast in bed the next day. The PDF states symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised in Greece.

Elounda SA's PDF lists the civil wedding documents it asks couples to supply (passports, birth certificates, certificate of no impediment, divorce or death certificates where relevant, two witnesses), each with an apostille and Greek translation, sent for approval at least four weeks before the wedding, and says the marriage must be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days. This is the venue's own guidance, not a government source.

Elounda SA lists reception food, beverage packages, open bars, dinner menus, entertainment and boat transfer as separate sections outside the ceremony packages (wedding reception, wedding dinner, beverages and additional services pages).

Nana Princess (Chersonissos, Crete) offers civil weddings on its private sandy beach, Greek Orthodox weddings in the private Chapel of St George on the hotel grounds, symbolic weddings officiated by a Nana Princess event coordinator, and vow renewals.
Nana Princess presents three wedding packages, Deluxe Dream, Ultimate Passion and Essential Elegance, and offers a bespoke package designed to the couple's requirements.

Nana Princess Deluxe Dream highlights: welcome drinks (homemade lemonade and berry water), champagne and chocolate strawberries in the honeymoon suite, and an event coordinator present throughout the stay.

Nana Princess Ultimate Passion highlights: a pre-wedding dinner tasting dishes from the wedding menu, a 30-minute massage the day before, and the bride escorted to the venue in a flower-decorated club car. Essential Elegance highlights: a private brunch at Eternal Blue for the couple and guests, an hour in the Royal Wellness Club private suite, and a farewell dinner for the couple.

Nana Princess symbolic weddings include a choice of decoration schemes with fresh flower arrangements, exclusive use of the chosen room or venue, the flower-decorated club car for the bride, and rose petals and rice for guests.

Nana Princess reception options: the Eternal Blue restaurant terrace, the poolside Meat-In-Point restaurant seating up to 120 guests, or the Conference Hall for a fully covered reception; served dinner or buffet.

Nana Princess says a dedicated event coordinator guides couples through local registry office requirements and other formalities after the date is booked. The page publishes a price for the vow renewal; drinks are not included in that renewal dinner.

Nana Princess recommends evening ceremonies because high-summer temperatures can reach 35 degrees C: 16:00 to 18:00 in April, May and October; 18:00 to 20:00 in June and September; 18:30 to 20:00 in July and August.

Abaton Island Resort & Spa (Crete) invites couples to choose from its wedding packages or create their own, and lists customisable elements: ceremony, music and entertainment, flowers, additional decor, beauty services, cocktail bar, wedding gala dinner, additional services and planning, photography and video.

Abaton 2025-2026 wedding brochure 'The Basics' lists ceremony, coordination services, photography, videography, Chiavari chairs, chair covers, table set-up decoration, bridal party flowers and a wedding arch, with a wedding coordinator preparing the details.

Abaton brochure lists additional services with indicative costs published (hair, make-up, spa, buttonholes, wedding cake, DJ, fireworks, centrepieces, rose petals, photographer, video), and publishes a venue fee for each venue (Elemes, Bony Fish, WOW, F-Zin, Ladies & Gentlemen, Buddha Bar, Open Air Theatre, Ballroom, Beach); the beach set-up fee is to be confirmed.

Abaton brochure terms: packages are subject to availability and do not include accommodation; packages are valid with a minimum accommodation booking of 10 rooms for a minimum of 2 nights (depending on guest numbers) and a minimum wedding reception of 20 guests, maximum capacity 300 guests; packages are complete and items are not interchangeable.

Abaton brochure publishes gala dinner buffet and set menus, cocktail reception menus, beverage packages and open bars, priced per person with minimum numbers for some; food and drink are booked separately from the ceremony basics.

Euphoria Resort offers three wedding options, Elxi, Pathos and Eros, for an informal wedding or renewal of vows, with a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel. The ceremony has two witnesses and the hotel's official representative.

Euphoria Elxi includes choice of hotel venue (beach or poolside), decoration with lanterns, petals, covered chairs and a table floral display, bouquet and buttonhole, petals and rice, sparkling wine and a single-tier cake with sugared almonds for up to 10 guests, pre-recorded ceremony music, 10 printed photographs from the hotel photographer and a wedding gift.

Euphoria Pathos adds sparkling wine and cake for up to 20 guests, a manicure and pedicure for the bride, a stocked minibar, a candlelit dinner for the couple with beverages, an anniversary dinner on return stays and the couple's own event coordinator.

Euphoria Eros adds canapes and a two-tier cake for up to 30 guests, a jazz musician at the ceremony, 20 photographs, a couple's massage, a four-course beach dinner with live music, champagne breakfast in bed, private check-in with welcome drinks for up to 30 guests, late check-out and the couple's own event coordinator.

Euphoria states its wedding options are complete packages whose items are not interchangeable, with no refund or alternative for unused services; packages can be customised at extra cost. Prices are published. Buffet, seated and cocktail receptions, beverage packages, open bars, custom cakes and entertainment are quoted separately on request.

Euphoria offers its honeymoon package free to couples who book any wedding package and stay at the hotel (welcome drink, sparkling wine and fruit, bed decoration, in-room breakfast, room upgrade on availability).

Grecotel Amirandes (near Heraklion, Crete) hosts weddings for up to 300 guests, with vows at its VIP Beach or chapel, a choice of dining venues and dedicated wedding specialists; it is 15 minutes from Heraklion International Airport. Its event page publishes no named wedding package; 'All-Inclusive' appears only as a hotel meal plan option.

Melenos Art Boutique Hotel (Lindos, Rhodes) hosts civil, symbolic and traditional Orthodox weddings and publishes no named package; its coordinators provide a schedule and costing sheet, organise tasks, outline a budget and build the itinerary.

Melenos says its wedding planner takes care of the legal documentation, including filing documents, marriage licence registration, and government and administrative fees, and official witnesses can be provided on request.
Melenos suggests reserving the entire hotel for a minimum of three nights; extra guests can stay at Melenos Apartments and Studios, about a 10-minute walk away in the village.

Melenos coordinators help with decor (garden flowers or a local florist; bouquets, corsages, centrepieces) and the reception menu; rehearsal dinner, welcome cocktail party, photographer and videographer, hair and make-up, private boat trip, live music and a candlelit dinner can be organised as additional services.

Atrium Prestige (south Rhodes) lists wedding venues including an amphitheatre near the beach, the Tsambika private chapel, Lachania private beach, Golden Dome, Panoramic Terrace, Thallassa restaurant and Kalithea main bar; it publishes no named wedding package.

Atrium Prestige's wedding specialist assists civil-ceremony couples with all arrangements to obtain the marriage licence. Listed services include a bridal villa suite, decoration and flowers, bridal make-up and hair, photography, bouquet, wedding cake, reception with menu tasting, DJ or live music and fireworks; symbolic ceremonies, elopements and vow renewals are offered.

Atrium Prestige gives a complimentary in-room welcome (fruit or sweets and sparkling wine) and a complimentary spa hydrobath for stays of 5 nights or more. Its 'Premium All-Inclusive' is a holiday offer, not a wedding package.

Angsana Corfu Resort & Spa (Corfu): the official Weddings & Honeymoons page offers a downloadable 2026 wedding brochure and says the resort's team plans the event; it does not name a wedding package or use the words 'all inclusive'. Ceremony venues in the brochure are listed under 'Symbolic Wedding Ceremony Venues'.

Angsana Corfu 2026 wedding brochure: symbolic ceremony venues are Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, up to 250 guests, mid-May to end of September, weather permitting) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, up to 30 guests, April to October, weather permitting).

Angsana Corfu 2026 wedding brochure: reception venues are Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, up to 250, end of May to end of September), Oribu Restaurant (indoor/outdoor, up to 150, April, May, September and October) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, up to 30, April to October).

Angsana Corfu 2026 brochure 'Special Wedding Offer': weddings booked at the resort earn a credit towards a future stay at a Banyan Tree or Angsana hotel, and weddings that meet a stated minimum food and beverage spend receive one complimentary night for the couple in a One-Bedroom Sea View Suite or Ionian Sea View Villa with private pool, a welcome amenity (champagne, fruit, traditional sweets) and in-room breakfast the day after the wedding. The minimum is stated as a money amount (not reproduced).

Corfu Imperial, Grecotel Exclusive Resort (Corfu): the official Weddings & Vow Renewals page (modified 19 March 2026) offers Yali Waterfront Restaurant, Aristos Restaurant (up to 50 guests) and the private islet 'Nissaki' (up to 50 guests), with dedicated wedding specialists, customised menus and trusted vendors. It names no package, lists no fixed inclusions and does not use 'all inclusive'; couples request a proposal by form.

Grand Resort Lagonissi (Athens Riviera, 40th km Athens-Sounion): the official weddings overview page (modified 26 September 2025) refers to 'special wedding packages' and 'exclusive wedding packages', a resort wedding planner who tailors the wedding, and events for up to 1,200 guests. It does not publish package names or contents and does not use 'all inclusive'.

Grand Resort Lagonissi 'Weddings & Ceremonies' page lists services: wedding assistance from the Events team, chefs and pastry chefs for cakes and desserts, floral and venue decoration designers, DJs with sound and lighting, photography, special effects and limousine rentals, a 'Honeymoon Suite', bridal treatments and beauty facilities, and private-pool dinners with a personal chef. Venues named: Uranus, Veghera, La Piscina, Aphrodite, Villa Elounda. The page does not say which services are included in a package and which are charged.

Grand Resort Lagonissi weddings brochure (PDF dated July 2022): the resort 'offers' the newlyweds their wedding-night stay as a gift in a honeymoon suite with fruit, treats, breakfast in bed and champagne; the site has a chapel (St Dimitrios) and the enquiry form asks whether the ceremony is in a church, the hotel's chapel or other. Venue capacities run from Galazia Akti (70 buffet, 100 set menu) to Uranus and Cosmos Ballroom (600 buffet, 700 set menu).

Costa Navarino (Messinia, Peloponnese): the official weddings page (modified 22 May 2026) says religious weddings can be held at the chapel of St Samson within Navarino Dunes or St Eleni at Navarino Agora, and civil ceremonies can be arranged on request indoors in town halls or outdoors on a beach, a boat, a hilltop or beside a stream. Weddings are handled by The Romanos, W Costa Navarino and Mandarin Oriental, Costa Navarino (eight spaces from 62 to 868 sqm). The page names no package and does not use 'all inclusive'.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens: the official wedding planning page lists 'Wedding Inclusions' for couples who book a wedding: one night of accommodation (wedding night), tailor-made amenities on the wedding night, a designed menu tasting for up to four guests, planning assistance from a dedicated in-house wedding specialist, a dedicated service team on the day, choice of venues, premium tables, chairs and linens, Sambonet silver and Rosenthal fine bone china, high-speed internet, and access to waterfront and garden locations as photography backdrops.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Athens: florals are arranged with preferred floral designers or the couple's own florist; the in-house salon offers hair, nails and make-up; the wedding specialist provides a list of recommended vendors (photographers, entertainers); private dining with exclusive use of one of four restaurants (Pelagos, Helios, Taverna 37, Mercato) is offered; catering spans a buffet for 50 to a gala dinner for 500. The page does not use 'all inclusive' and does not describe a named package.

Myconian Collection (Elia, Mykonos): the official weddings page (modified 28 September 2026) says it can either prepare the stage for the couple's own team or provide a complete event solution covering invitations, travel logistics, menus, specialist cakes, wines, flowers, favours, lighting, sound and music, honeymoon planning and fireworks. It names no package and does not use 'all inclusive'.

Myconian Collection: ceremonies can be held in a small whitewashed chapel with a reception on the beach or in a restaurant; the team assists with officiating ceremonies across all denominations, has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for Indian cuisine; the Horizons Ballroom seats 270 at rounds, 380 to 400 banquet-style and up to 550 for cocktails.

Astir of Paros (Kolymbithres, Naoussa, Paros): the official weddings page (last modified 5 November 2018) offers a wedding ceremony and reception with the executive chef's menus, decoration and personalised service. It publishes no package names, inclusions or exclusions.

Grace Hotel (Auberge Collection, Imerovigli) charges a flat venue fee. For celebrations over 50 people it includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, tables and chairs for dining, lounge furniture and bars, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, event set-up and breakdown, event staffing, screens and room dividers, and transport between the hotel and the event site for guests staying overnight at Grace Hotel.

Grace Hotel: for weddings of 50 guests or fewer the flat venue fee includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, tables and chairs for dining, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, a wedding arbour, event set-up and breakdown, and transport to and from the event site.

Grace Hotel's 'Furniture & Linens' note says custom tables, dining chairs, lounge furniture, glassware, china, silverware, white, navy or black napkins, set-up and breakdown, bartenders, event staffing and screens and room dividers are included in the facility fee.

Grace Hotel provides a dedicated event manager for venue details, but a wedding planner is required for all weddings and should be involved for a minimum of 3 months before the wedding; at the 363 Lounge the decor and seating are looked after by the couple's wedding coordinator.

Grace Hotel menus: for parties of up to 30 guests, offering an onsite choice of three pre-selected main courses is 'for a charge', with a minimum four-course menu; events over 30 guests may also select three main courses.

Grace Hotel accommodation: guests may book individually; for a room block or resort buyout the Sales Manager quotes on dates, rooms and room nights; the hotel does not require a minimum number of rooms. A DJ or live band is allowed (the hotel gives recommendations) and a private lounge with full-length mirror is available to the wedding party from 8am. Capacities: 363 Lounge 40 seated / 60 standing; The Villa 15 seated / 60 standing.

Canaves Collection (Oia) weddings page offers 'Wedding Package Options' via a downloadable wedding brochure; its enquiry form lists ceremony types Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal, and optional extras such as flower arch, gazebo, bouquets, wedding crowns, bombonieres, photographer, videographer, wedding cake, fireworks, 'Preparation of Wedding Documents', DJ, live bands, harpist and lighting (enquiry options, not stated package inclusions).

Canaves wedding brochure: the Panorama Balcony / Caldera Arches 'Wedding Ceremony & Dinner Reception for up to 30 guests' package (Canaves Oia Suites) includes private use of the ceremony and reception area for up to 5 hours (until 11:30pm), event planning services, recorded music of the couple's choice, a glass of sparkling wine for the toast, basic set-up (chairs, tables, white tablecloths, silverware), a two-tier wedding cake, and music up to 60 dB until 11:30pm. A room booking is not required but is recommended.

Canaves wedding brochure lists a Panorama Balcony 'Elopement for couple only' package with the same inclusions (5 hours private use until 11:30pm, event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up, two-tier cake, music up to 60 dB). Caldera Arches dinner layouts: one long table for up to 25 or three tables for up to 30; the Panorama Balcony dinner reception is for up to 12.

Canaves wedding brochure: the Veranda (Canaves Sunday) ceremony and reception package for up to 40 guests includes private use for up to 5 hours (until 11pm), event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up, two-tier cake and music up to 60 dB until 11pm. Room requirement: up to 20 guests must book two suites for at least three nights; 21 to 40 guests requires a buyout of Canaves Sunday under special terms.

Canaves wedding brochure, Canaves Epitome: Sunset Terrace package (couple only or up to 25 guests; up to 5 hours until 11pm, music up to 60 dB) requires one room for at least three nights for 8 to 25 guests; Sunset Terrace and Elements Restaurant (26 to 45 guests; 7 hours until 1am, music up to 70 dB) requires three rooms for three nights; Sunset Terrace, Pool Area and Elements (45 to 100 guests) requires four rooms (45-60), six rooms (60-80), a half buyout of 25 rooms (80-100) and a full buyout of 53 rooms above 100 guests, each with three-night minimums. All include event planning services, recorded music, sparkling wine toast, basic set-up and two-tier cake.

Canaves wedding brochure payment terms: a non-refundable deposit (stated as a percentage of the venue cost) secures the venue and starts planning; the balance is due one month before the event with the food and beverage cost; venue payments are always non-refundable and vendor cancellation fees follow each vendor's contract. Food and beverage menus are separate ('Explore our menus'). The brochure says weddings can be real or symbolic and an in-house wedding planner handles details.

Canaves Exclusives & Buyouts page: full-property buyouts of Canaves Epitome (53 rooms, max 170 guests), Canaves Oia Suites (48 rooms, 120), Canaves Ena (18 rooms, 45) and Canaves Sunday (10 rooms, 22), quoted through a 'Request Your Buyout Proposal' form; no buyout inclusions are published. Venue table: Epitome Outdoor Gardens theatre 180 / banquet 250 / reception 280; Omnia Pool Area 100/150/250; Sunset Terrace 100/80/100.

Santorini Gem (caldera venue plus wedding villa) offers a downloadable 'Rental Packages 2026' brochure and says it can host large or smaller events in outdoor and indoor spaces with selected services and a variety of menus, plus wedding planning services. The home page publishes a promotional discount on the venue rental fee for new 2027 bookings (figure not recorded).

Santorini Gem Rental Packages 2026 lists a Ceremony Wedding Terrace Exclusive Hire (morning, event 10:30-11:30, bridal room from 10:15) with a white altar table, chandelier, lanterns, white Tiffany chairs, sound system, guest and accessible facilities and a bridal suite; a wooden gazebo with curtains is 'at an extra cost'; a per-extra-guest fee applies beyond the base group and children under 12 are complimentary. Prices are published in the PDF (not recorded).

Santorini Gem Rental Packages 2026: three Ceremony & Reception packages on the upper terrace and pool area (event 17:00-01:30): venue only; venue plus villa day use (12 noon to 01:30); venue plus villa overnight (12 noon to 10am next day). Included equipment: altar table, chandelier, lanterns with candles, white Tiffany chairs, sound system, round or rectangle tables, linen, plating, cutlery, accessible facilities, air-conditioned bridal room, in-house catering facilities and bar; gazebo 'at an extra cost'; an earlier start is charged per hour. Rental fees are published in euros (not recorded).

Santorini Gem villa hospitality (per Rental Packages 2026): 5 bedrooms sleeping 8, a welcome sparkling wine and seasonal fruit, mineral water, mini bar, linen, night security and breakfast for the couple and villa guests; breakfast for more friends is at additional cost. The villa page says five bedrooms for up to eight guests, four bathrooms, two living rooms, a private pool and gardens (bathroom count differs from the PDF's five).
facts.conflicts: Villa bathrooms: villa page says four, Rental Packages 2026 PDF says five.

facts.claim: Santorini Gem Venue Policy 2027-2028: all couples must have a wedding planner; the venue provides its standard set-up; set-up from 1pm on the day; no storage; the venue does not provide guest transport and guests must pre-book their own; music up to 80 dB, lowered to listening level at 11pm and off 15 minutes before the end time; bar closes 30 minutes before the end; confetti, plate smashing and flying lanterns not permitted.

Santorini Gem Venue Policy dining: Ceremony & Reception packages require choosing a set menu (20 adults minimum, 80 maximum) or a buffet (over 30 guests, poolside receptions buffet only); personalised menus may carry supplementary fees; set menus are starter, salad, main and dessert with wedding cake not included; open bar packages are optional but if chosen apply to all adults (and a children's open bar then applies); tips are not included in menu prices; no outside food or drink.

Santorini Gem Venue Policy booking terms: a non-refundable deposit of the rental fee secures the date, the rental balance is due 9 months before the wedding, and the food and beverage order must be final and paid 40 days before; a postponement handling fee applies and postponement is only to the following season; ceremony options on the booking form are 'Civil or Symbolic ceremony only', ceremony and reception, or ceremony, reception and villa overnight. Monetary figures and percentages are published (not recorded).

Andronis 2026 wedding brochure 'Andronis Wedding Package' lists: preparation of the documents for the marriage licence, a marriage certificate issued in Greek, coordination and booking of the ceremony date and time with the Mayor (two witnesses required), floral decor for the ceremony, bridal bouquet and boutonniere, a two-tier wedding cake, a bottle of sparkling wine with chocolate-covered strawberries, a private cliffside ceremony area, Andronis Heart koufeta favours, a symbolic gift, and a romantic turndown with sparkling wine and strawberries.

Andronis brochure ceremony venues: Heart Pool and Grande Pool (Andronis Arcadia, Oia) and Lycabettus Restaurant cliff area (Andronis Luxury Suites, ceremonies 10:00-17:00, last at 16:00) each include two glasses of prosecco, koufeta and a jar of honey with walnuts, with prosecco for up to two additional guests charged separately. Receptions: Pacman Restaurant and Miltos' Greek Table offer full exclusivity or semi-private use by season; Lycabettus full exclusivity up to 40 guests and cliff area up to 20, with a curated degustation menu.

Andronis brochure a la carte services: concierge-assisted marriage registration at the Town Hall, round-trip Town Hall transfers, photography (1 hour, 50 images) and videography (2 hours, 3-7 minute edit), extra hours, hair and make-up, and musicians on request; officiant, florals, photography sessions, fireworks and other bespoke services 'can be arranged upon request at an additional charge'. Services also listed: wedding planner, flower decoration, photography and spa rituals.
Andronis Weddings & Celebrations page links the 2026 wedding brochure and an enquiry form (event types Wedding, Birthday, Anniversary, Dining Event).

Vedema, a Luxury Collection Resort (Megalochori), states on its Marriott events page that it provides wedding services; ceremonies can be held at the resort, on the beach or elsewhere, with receptions at the Pool Restaurant or, for more privacy, the Canava Wine Bar; a private beach bonfire and barbecue are also offered.
Vedema's events page says its 400-year-old wine cellar can hold up to 120 guests for a banquet and 150 for a reception; its Thira Conference Center is listed at 75 (theatre).

Vedema's events page says a dedicated Celebration Consultant will arrange local support services, photographer and videographer, custom floral arrangements for the bride and venue, wedding cake and musical entertainment; optional arrangements include personalised menus and private dining, a horse-drawn carriage and fireworks.

Vedema's events page says the resort attends to 'all of the legal documents necessary to marry on Santorini' and can provide flowers, music or DJ, hairdresser, make-up artist, spa treatments, photographer and videographer and customised food and wine menus; its Elios Spa's two salon suites can be reserved together for the bridal party on the wedding day.

Vedema's events page publishes per-person catering prices for events (amounts not recorded here) and a separate Honeymoon Package that includes a complimentary candlelit dinner, a signature honeymoon amenity and flower bed decoration.

Ikos Aria on Kos hosts weddings: its wedding page says the resort's event planner team and a devoted wedding planner plan and coordinate the event, from coordinating the legal arrangements with the local Town Hall to arranging accommodation for up to 30 guests, and couples can choose from packages featuring touches from wedding cakes to romantic dinners.

Ikos Aria's Special Wedding package lists: reservation of the wedding venue date and time; wedding planning and coordination; assistance in submitting the documents for a civil wedding; help to receive the marriage certificate after the civil wedding; a wedding cake to serve 10 people; rose petals in the room on the wedding day. Couples staying for their honeymoon also receive a romantic dinner, a farewell gift and a welcome bottle of sparkling wine.

Ikos Aria's wedding page says vows can be read in designated wedding spots in the resort grounds; a legal ceremony needs officially translated legal documents and two witnesses of legal age, and couples should contact the Greek consulate in their home country about paperwork, as the Greek government sets the requirements.

The Ikos Resorts site describes its Greek resorts, including Ikos Aria on Kos, as stays where 'everything is included in your stay' (the resort's all-inclusive holiday concept); the wedding page does not state that the wedding package itself is all inclusive.

Euphoria Resort is a five-star, Ultra All Inclusive family beach resort on the seashore of Kolymvari, about 14 miles west of Chania, with 344 rooms and suites (including a 70-key Signature Collection) on a 65,000 sq m sea-front property, a 3,500 sq m pool area and a 1,500 sq m spa. A member of EM Resorts (the same group as Minoa Palace).
facts.conflicts: Same homepage gives the drive from Chania International Airport (CHQ) as 30 minutes (meta description) and 40 minutes (body text). [[VERIFY: Euphoria Resort transfer time from Chania Airport, 30 or 40 minutes]]

facts.claim: Euphoria Resort (Kolymvari, Chania, Crete) offers three wedding options (Elxi, Pathos, Eros) for 'an informal wedding or renewal of vows'; each includes a choice of hotel venues (beaches and poolside), venue decoration (lanterns, petals, covered chairs, floral table display), bouquet and buttonhole, two witnesses and the hotel's official representative, 'a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel', petals and rice, sparkling wine and a wedding cake after the ceremony (for up to 10, 20 or 30 guests by option), ceremony music (pre-recorded, or a jazz musician in Eros), photographs from the hotel photographer and a gift. Pathos and Eros add spa treatments, dinners and 'your own event coordinator'. Re-checked live; restates crete fact_400/401.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_302) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages (a statement of no record of a previous marriage, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate); local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. It says each country decides what proof it accepts and there may be different regional and national laws. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_303) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to marry, too closely related, or forced to marry.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_304) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation of signatures and/or seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is needed for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; apostilled documents and CNIs are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged in advance, or can be returned by mail. The Embassy gives no legal advice, does not witness signatures on overseas documents, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and a fee applies (amounts not recorded). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, shown as still current when read live 11 November 2026 UTC). It notes Greece is in an active seismic zone with earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near Santorini, and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period, June to September.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice says Greece is in the Schengen area; Australians can make short trips without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and on arrival for a short stay on an Australian passport you register fingerprints and a photo under the European Entry/Exit System (EES), which is free and needs no action before arrival, though it may cause delays at borders. Depending on why you are travelling and how long you stay you may need a visa, and entry conditions can change at short notice, so contact the nearest Greek embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

insider_details.detail: On Crete, the named packages are ceremony bundles, not whole weddings: Elounda SA, Abaton and Euphoria all list reception food, drinks and open bars separately, so compare the ceremony package and the dinner quote side by side.
Read the 'not interchangeable' line: Abaton and Euphoria say package items cannot be swapped, and Euphoria gives no refund for unused items, so drop what you won't use before you sign, not after.

Room minimums sit inside the package terms: Elounda SA asks for at least three nights for the couple, Abaton for ten rooms over two nights and Melenos suggests a whole-hotel booking for three nights, so price the room block with the package.

A symbolic package is the simplest to run but has no legal effect in Greece (Elounda SA says so outright); couples wanting a legal marriage pair it with a civil ceremony, and Euphoria's three options are informal only.
Plan the ceremony for early evening in summer: Nana Princess itself recommends 18:30 to 20:00 in July and August because of heat and UV.

Paperwork help is a venue offer, not a promise of the result: Elounda SA includes licence coordination but charges the Municipal or Metropolis fee on top, while Melenos says government and administrative fees are attended to by its planner, so ask each venue which fees sit inside the quote.

Of the Corfu, mainland and Mykonos venues read, none calls its wedding offer 'all inclusive'; the closest to a published inclusion list is Four Seasons Astir Palace, so ask every other venue for its inclusions in writing.

Angsana Corfu's ceremonies are symbolic and its biggest terrace runs only from mid or late May to end of September, so shoulder-season couples should plan around Oribu Restaurant or the smaller garden.
Several venues offer the couple's wedding night or a perk tied to spend (Four Seasons, Angsana, Lagonissi), so check whether that night is part of the quote or a separate offer with conditions.
Costa Navarino and Grand Resort Lagonissi both have chapels on site, and Costa Navarino also arranges civil ceremonies on request; couples confirm church and civil paperwork requirements themselves.
Myconian Collection works either as a full-service provider or as a stage for an outside team, so decide early which model you want before comparing quotes.
